longTitle: Social Security at 62, 67 or 70? The Break-Even Ages, From SSA's Own Data
sources: Sources: Social Security Administration — 2027 COLA Fact Sheet; Annual Statistical Supplement 2026, Table 6.B5.1; Office of the Chief Actuary, 2023 period life table (2026 Trustees Report); early retirement reduction, delayed retirement credits, survivor benefits and the retirement earnings test. Break-even ages, totals and probabilities are our calculations (today's dollars, before taxes, no investment returns).
music_credits: Music by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0.

clips.title: Social Security at 62 vs 70: 77% more per month #Shorts
clips.desc: Full benefit $2,000 at 67 → $1,400 at 62 or $2,480 at 70 (SSA rules, born 1960+).

clips.hook: Almost half used to claim at *62*
clips.title: Half of retirees claimed Social Security at 62. Now? #Shorts
clips.desc: 2008: ~45% of new retirees started at 62. 2024: ~23%. At 70+: 1.5% → 9% (SSA Annual Statistical Supplement 2026).
